blogs.title: If you are writing Lakeflow Pipelines in Databricks, it’s time to update your imports.
blogs.summary: Databricks is phasing out legacy @dlt decorators in favor of Apache Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) using pyspark.pipelines (dp). Here is why the shift matters.
blogs.content:
Databricks is phasing out the legacy @dlt decorators and dlt module in favor of Apache Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP), using pyspark.pipelines (conventionally imported as dp).

🔄 The Evolution from @dlt to dp

The Old Pattern: Using import dlt tied pipeline logic tightly to proprietary Delta Live Tables syntax and runtime constructs.

The New Standard: Using import pyspark.pipelines as dp standardizes declarative data engineering directly within the broader Apache Spark and Lakeflow ecosystem.

⚡ What Changes in Your Code?

The shift is straightforward and keeps the declarative style you're used to:

  • import dlt → import pyspark.pipelines as dp
  • @dlt.table → @dp.table
  • @dlt.view → @dp.view
  • dlt.read() / dlt.read_stream() → dp.read() / dp.read_stream()

Expectations syntax now standardizes under the new dp module decorators (like @dp.expect, @dp.expect_or_drop, and @dp.expect_or_fail).

💡 Why This Matters

  • Closer Alignment with Open Standards: Standardizing declarative pipelines under pyspark bridges the gap between proprietary platform code and open-source Spark paradigms.
  • Core to Lakeflow: Powers next-gen Lakeflow Pipelines with clean lifecycle management, automated orchestration, and built-in Unity Catalog governance.
  • Seamless Transition: It’s a clean 1:1 conceptual mapping, making modernization of existing DLT notebooks fast and painless.

📚 Reference doc: Databricks Documentation

blogs.title: Optimizing Azure Databricks Cluster Costs in Telecom Delta Lake
blogs.summary: Key strategies for auto-scaling, spot instances, and Delta Lake Z-Ordering to drastically reduce compute costs on multi-terabyte workloads.
blogs.content:
Processing multi-terabyte daily telecom feeds on Azure Databricks can quickly explode cloud compute costs if cluster configurations are left unoptimized. Here are the core architectural patterns I implemented at Amdocs for Three UK to streamline cost efficiency.

1. Auto-Scaling with Single-Node & Spot Instances

For batch ETL jobs running during off-peak hours, leveraging Azure Spot VMs for worker nodes can reduce compute costs by up to 70-80%. Combined with tight auto-scaling thresholds, clusters scale down immediately when task queues drain.

# Example PySpark Delta Table Optimization
spark.sql("""
  OPTIMIZE delta.`/mnt/telecom/cdr_fact`
  ZORDER BY (account_id, event_timestamp)
""")

2. Delta Lake Liquid Clustering vs Z-Ordering

Traditional partitioning on high-cardinality keys leads to the small file problem. By switching to Delta Lake Z-Ordering or Liquid Clustering on frequent join keys (like Account ID and MSISDN), scan volumes drop significantly, leading to faster execution times and lower DBU consumption.

3. Key Takeaways

  • Set aggressive auto-termination timeouts (e.g. 15-20 minutes) on interactive developer clusters.
  • Enforce Unity Catalog table ACLs to prevent redundant compute query scans.
  • Use Delta Live Tables (DLT) for automated pipeline maintenance and data quality checks.

blogs.title: High-Throughput PySpark & Snowflake ELT Architecture
blogs.summary: Designing parallelized Spark-to-Snowflake connectors and presentation data marts for enterprise BI tools like Adobe Analytics & Medallia.
blogs.content:
Modern enterprise analytics requires decoupling raw data lake storage from presentation data marts. Integrating Azure Databricks PySpark pipelines with Snowflake DWH creates a robust, highly parallelized analytics engine.

1. Optimizing the Spark-Snowflake Connector

When staging data into Snowflake, using Azure Blob Storage as an intermediate staging area allows Spark to perform bulk COPY operations directly into Snowflake virtual warehouses, avoiding single-row insert bottlenecks.

# High-performance Snowflake write configuration
df.write \
  .format("snowflake") \
  .options(**sf_options) \
  .option("dbtable", "PRESENTATION.CUSTOMER_360") \
  .option("usestagingtable", "ON") \
  .mode("overwrite") \
  .save()

2. Dimensional Modeling & Presentation Layer

By enforcing a clean Medallion Architecture (Bronze -> Silver -> Gold), downstream Snowflake data marts (Adobe Customer Survey, Salesforce extracts) receive pre-validated, dimensional models ready for instant querying.
